symbols.name: selected chunk count
symbols.meaning: The number of address chunks in which the same bit position is selected; a count.
symbols.quote: Let $D$ be the number of selected address chunks.

symbols.name: chunk bound
symbols.meaning: An upper bound on the number of selected chunks $D$; a count.
symbols.quote: Let $d$ be an upper bound on $D$, so $D\le d$.

symbols.name: chunk width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each address chunk; a count.
symbols.quote: Let $K$ be the number of bits in each chunk.

symbols.name: stored bit volume
symbols.meaning: The number of stored bits in the array; a count.
symbols.quote: Let $V$ be the number of stored bits.

symbols.name: cost exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed exponent below 1 in the layer's cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$.

symbols.name: butterfly
symbols.meaning: The map $H_0(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2)$ applied to each selected bit.
symbols.quote: Fast simultaneous butterfly layers is a fixed-tape procedure that applies the butterfly $H_0(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2)$ to one bit position in several address chunks at once.

symbols.name: bit-flip matrix
symbols.meaning: The two-by-two matrix that swaps the two basis vectors of one bit.

symbols.name: phase matrix
symbols.quote: Let $\mathsf S$ be the diagonal phase matrix $\operatorname{diag}(1,i)$.

symbols.name: two-point kernel
symbols.meaning: The two-by-two kernel $\tfrac12((1+i)I+(1-i)X)$ from which each butterfly is built.

relations.quote: The layer gets its exponent $\lambda'<1$ from [Recursive power saving from s<Wm](recursive-power-saving.md), since each recursive call uses fewer calls on less volume.
The layer moves whole chunks by [Fast interchange of address fields](fast-address-interchange.md) to bring each group of selected bits to a common offset.
The layer is built from the root multiplications of [Synthetic polynomial transforms](synthetic-transforms.md), which are signed shifts.
The layer's single truncation is bounded as in [Fixed-point precision and exact recovery](fixed-point-precision.md).
